s10.old: **F3: a shipped regression the audit caught.** First attempt made party columns count `Support Activity` (24E/24F) only. Wrong: **24K, 24Z, 24C, 24P, 24R, 24H are all money FOR the candidate** and are the ordinary corporate-PAC case. That stripped **$151.4M** out of party columns (Perdue 2022 Bakkt: $2,995,566 -> $0, coverage 100% -> 0%), turned `Other / Unclassified` into a **$1.99B/$2.55B opposition dump**, and left two different coverage denominators in one workbook (Sherrod Brown 100.0% vs 0.6%, 3 rows >100%). **Shipped design = four buckets summing to the total:** Dem/Rep = `Downstream − Oppose` for that party; Oppose gets its own column; Other/Unclassified means genuinely non-D/R; Party Coverage divides by the mixed total on BOTH the summary and focused sheets. Integrity asserts `Downstream − Dem − Rep − Other − Oppose = 0` (a real check: Oppose from R, Downstream from an Excel SUMIFS). Focused sheets subtract opposition via a **Section-guarded** SUMIFS; without the guard every beneficiary row reports CHECK (74 on Crypto). **Also NOT an invariant:** `Support + Oppose <= Downstream`: FEC correction/refund rows are negative and carry neither direction code, so they pull the unsigned total below the components (272/2,979 CU rows, all residuals negative, to -$735,710). Don't re-add that assertion.
s10.why: "below the components" is a number comparison
